Heard Mr. Suryasanta Mohapatra, learned counsel for the Petitioner and Mr. Rabi Narayan Mishra, learned counsel for the State.

3. This Writ Petition has been filed by the Petitioner for inaction of the Opposite Party No.1-Collector-cum- District Magistrate, Jagatsinghpur for initiating arbitration under Section 3G of the National Highways Act, 1956 on the grievance of the Petitioner for enhancement of compensation.

entities.text: Opposite Party No.1-Collector-cum- District Magistrate, Jagatsinghpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel for the Petitioner drew the attention of this Court to Annexure-4 which is the letter dated 16.08.2024 of the Sub-Collector, Jagatsinghpur (Grievance Cell), Opposite Party No.3 wherein it is mentioned that vide official letter No.2851 dated 15.07.2023, the matter has been referred to the Opposite Party No.1 for necessary action.

Learned counsel submitted that the Petitioner has submitted a representation vide Annexure-3 before Opposite Party No.1 for initiation of the arbitration proceeding but no response has been received from the Collector regarding initiation of such proceeding and the application is pending as such and therefore, necessary direction to be issued to the Opposite Party to do the needful for initiation of the arbitration proceeding under Section 3G of the said Act, which is as follows:-
"3G. Determination of amount payable as compensation.--(1) Where any land is acquired under this Act, there shall be paid an amount which shall be determined by an order of the competent authority.
Bhabani Shankar Das vs Collector-Cum-District .... Opp. ... on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45292922/
1 (2) Where the right of user or any right in the nature of an easement on, any land is acquired under this Act, there shall be paid an amount to the owner and any other person whose right of enjoyment in that land has been affected in any manner whatsoever by reason of such acquisition an amount calculated at ten per cent, of the amount determined under sub- section (1), for that land.
(3) Before proceeding to determine the amount under sub-section (1) or sub-section (2), the competent authority shall give a public notice published in two local newspapers, one of which will be in a vernacular language inviting claims from all persons interested in the land to be acquired.
(4) Such notice shall state the particulars of the land and shall require all persons interested in such land to appear in person or by an agent or by a legal practitioner referred to in sub-section (2) of section 3C, before the competent authority, at a time and place and to state the nature of their respective interest in such land.

(5) If the amount determined by the competent authority under sub-section (1) or sub-section (2) is not acceptable to either of the parties, the amount shall, on an application by either of the parties, be determined by the arbitrator to be appointed by the Central Government-- (6) Subject to the provisions of this Act, the provisions of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 (26 of 1996) shall apply to every arbitration under this Act.

Since the matter has been referred for the arbitration to the Opposite Party No.1 on 15.07. 2023 vide letter No.2851 and the application of the Petitioner is also pending in that respect, let the Collector take necessary decision in initiating the arbitration proceeding under Section 3G of the Bhabani Shankar Das vs Collector-Cum-District .... Opp

2 National Highways Act, 1956 within a period of four weeks from the date of production of the certified copy of the order and then after appearance of the parties, dispose of the arbitration proceeding within three months.
The decision taken in the arbitration proceeding shall be communicated to the Petitioner by the Collector-cum-District Magistrate, Jagatsinghpur within two weeks of taking the decision.
The Writ Petition is disposed of accordingly.
